newsitem.title: CROATIA: Heavy snow surprises Croatia's Adriatic coast.
newsitem.headline: Heavy snow surprises Croatia's Adriatic coast.

text.p: A thick coat of dry snow, unlike anything seen in 20 years, covered much of Croatia's central Adriatic coast and its islands on Sunday after a freak blizzard, state radio said.
The Dalmatian seaboard of Croatia is better known for its Mediterranean climate with mild rainy winters and strong winds. Snow virtually never falls because of above-zero temperatures.
Thick flurries lent the atmosphere of a proper continental winter and residents in the main port of Split were excited.

"I don't remember such a thick snow for some 20 years now. It's at least 10 centimetres thick. It looks like we're somewhere on the (central European) continent," said Edi Mise at Split's municipal information centre.

"There is really heavy snow here," said Reuters cameraman Pasko Bacic. "It is like nothing I can remember," he added and went to join his children eager to try their hand at making snowballs and snowmen.
They did not have much time, as forecasters said temperatures would rise and snow turn to rain on Monday.
The unusual weather grounded Split air traffic until the afternoon. Some international trains were several hours late.
Strong northern winds toppled 180 electricity poles in the Zadar area and on Pag island, leaving parts of the town and surrounding villages without power or telephone links.
State radio reported snow and sub-zero temperatures in other main Dalmatian towns including Sibenik and Zadar and on the islands of Solta, Hvar and Brac.
Hoteliers on Hvar, nicknamed the "Island of Sun", had advertised a free stay for tourists if snow fell.
